| A18 | **Player view: a selected body's framing gradually retreated while time was running.** Reported 2026-07-31 — "the camera drifts away", "only if time is running", which is the whole diagnosis in five words: the body was moving and the camera was not. **Root cause, one line in `driveFocus` (`lib/holo/scene.ts`).** Once the focus ease expired, the FREE-HEADING (3D) branch did only `controls.target.lerp(desiredTarget, 0.08)` — it re-aimed at the body and left `camera.position` exactly where it stood, with a comment calling that "the natural hologram feel". Turning to track reads well for a second and then fails: a body orbiting AWAY from a fixed camera is further away every frame, so the shot silently retreated until the planet was a dot. Rotating in place cannot hold a distance; only travelling with the body can. Note the LOCKED-heading branch was always correct — it re-seats the camera at `target + heading * d` every frame — so this only ever affected rotatable 3D presets, which is every Holo Table. **Fix:** carry the target→camera offset with the body (`followOffset = camera.position - target`, copy the target onto the body, replace the camera at `target + followOffset`). Preserving the OFFSET is what keeps everything else working: dragging still orbits the body, the wheel still changes distance, the turntable still spins, and a re-click still re-frames through the ladder because that arms `focusDrive` and eases to the new distance above. The target is copied rather than lerped, matching the locked branch — a lerp lags a fast-moving moon off centre. **Verified live** on a broadcast player view (Altair IV focused, clock at 1 month/s): centre-frame ink held at 1131-1774 over ~11 simulated months with no downward trend, where the old behaviour collapsed it to ~12 as the body left frame. Confirmed visually by Alex on the same running view. | fixed v2.1.313-beta |
| A19 | **Player view at 1:1 scale AND 1:1 distances: small bodies far out jitter — the orbit line vibrates and a moon does not sit on it.** Reported 2026-07-31, using Pluto/Charon as the example, and explicitly flagged as edge-of-the-envelope: it needs BOTH dials at their honest end, which is the regime A9 opened up (v2.1.297-303). Not diagnosed yet. **Where to start.** The 2D orrery solved exactly this and the fix is documented — `SystemVisualizer` uses a **Floating Origin (relative camera)** pattern, doing its arithmetic in 64-bit JS relative to the current camera focus before handing coordinates to the renderer, precisely because large absolute distances lose precision in a 32-bit rendering matrix (see `docs/dev/ARCHITECTURE.md`). The holo scene has no equivalent: it compresses map/AU distances into scene units and then leaves three.js to build float32 matrices, so a body 40 AU out drawn at its true radius is a tiny object at a huge coordinate — the worst case for float32, and it would show up as exactly this, a vibrating orbit line and a satellite that will not stay glued to its primary. **Two candidates, and they are separable:** (a) float32 precision in the world/view matrices, which the floating-origin treatment fixes; (b) the true-scale screen-space floor (`updateTrueScaleFloor`, A9/v2.1.297+) resizing a sub-pixel body per frame, which could make the body and its orbit line disagree about where the centre is. Check (b) first — it is cheap to rule out by pausing the floor — before taking on (a), which is a real piece of work.  **CHEAP CANDIDATE RULED OUT, v2.1.316-beta — and by construction, not by sampling.** The A9 screen-space floor (`updateTrueScaleFloor`, `holo/scene.ts:1086`) writes `b.mesh.scale` and NOTHING else. Scaling a mesh about its own origin cannot translate its centre, so it cannot make a body and its orbit line disagree about where that centre is. Confirmed by checking every write to a body's position in the scene: they are all in `updatePositions` (:1866/:1868/:1871) and `updateSurfaceConstructs` (:1992), none of them in the floor. Nor can the floor cause the vibration: `k = minPx / pxR` sets the rendered radius to exactly `minPx`, so the pinned size is stable by construction rather than a feedback loop that could hunt. **So it is the expensive one.** The remaining candidate is float32 precision in the GPU's world/view matrices, which is exactly what a body 40 AU out drawn at its true radius provokes: a tiny object at a huge coordinate, where neighbouring vertices differ in the last bits a float32 has. That fits both symptoms at once — an orbit line whose vertices round differently frame to frame VIBRATES, and a moon placed by a separate per-frame path rounds differently again, so it will not sit on the line. It also fits the trigger: it needs BOTH dials at their honest end, because that is when scene coordinates get large while radii get tiny. **What the fix involves.** A Floating Origin, which the 2D orrery already does and documents — do the arithmetic in 64-bit JS RELATIVE TO THE CAMERA, and hand the renderer only small numbers (`ARCHITECTURE.md`, `SystemVisualizer`). In the holo that means rebasing the scene on the current focus: body positions, the static orbit-ring vertex buffers (which are built once in absolute scene units and would need rebuilding, or a per-object offset, when the origin moves), the belts, and anything else holding absolute coordinates. It is a real piece of work with a re-render cost, and it wants its own scoped session — NOT this batch.  **QUANTIFIED 2026-07-31 — the numbers say it outright.** At TRUE scale `compressScalar` is linear: `scene = GRID_RADIUS * r / rMax` = `12 * r / 39.5` for Sol, so Pluto sits at scene coordinate 12. float32 has a 24-bit mantissa, so the gap between representable values at magnitude 12 is `2^-20` = **9.54e-7 scene units**. Against that: Charon's orbit radius is 3.98e-5 scene units = **42 ULP** — a whole orbit quantised to about 42 steps per axis, which is why it will not sit smoothly on its line — and Pluto's own RADIUS is 2.41e-6 = **2.5 ULP**, i.e. the body is essentially inside the rounding error before the screen-space floor inflates it for display. Every camera nudge re-rounds, which is the vibration. It gets worse, not better, on a map whose outermost body is further out. **Rebasing fixes it by orders of magnitude:** with the origin on Pluto, Charon's coordinates are ~4e-5, where the ULP is 3.6e-12 — about **1e7 ULP of headroom** instead of 42. **Design notes for whoever takes it.** (1) There is ONE choke point: every absolute→scene conversion goes through `positionToScene` (`holo/scene.ts:725`, 8 call sites). (2) Rebase AFTER the compression, not before — `compressScalar` is a RADIAL, nonlinear map, so a translation does not commute with it; subtracting the focus's COMPRESSED scene position is a pure translation of the rendered space and composes cleanly. (3) Moon orbit rings are ALREADY safe: `buildMoonOrbitRing` stores vertices relative to the parent and the loop is positioned at the parent, so its numbers are small by construction. The absolute holders that would need re-emitting on a rebase are `buildOrbitRing` (heliocentric), the belts, and the grid. (4) The camera and `controls.target` rebase with everything else. **Verification it should be held to:** assert that Charon's RENDERED offset from Pluto matches the propagated offset at true scale — today it will not — and measure frame-to-frame stability of the orbit-line vertices across a slow camera move. Both are numeric, like C3's. **FIXED v2.1.319-beta — a floating origin, rebased on the camera's focus.** Root cause in a sentence: the heliocentric orbit rings and the grid are static float32 vertex buffers holding ABSOLUTE scene coordinates, and at true scale those are magnitude 12, where a float32 step is 9.5e-7 — so the line's SHAPE is quantised at that step, and the shader then adds that large vertex to a large, oppositely-signed modelView translation, a cancellation that re-rounds every time the camera moves. **A correction to the earlier diagnosis, and it changes what you should look at.** The MOON was never misplaced. three.js builds `modelViewMatrix` on the CPU in float64 and only then hands it to the GPU, so a body's centre arrives as a SMALL camera-space translation, accurate to ~1e-12; every body position in this scene is a float64 JS number all the way. So "a moon will not sit on its line" is the LINE being wrong, not the moon — which is also why the moon reads as steady while the line vibrates against it. The cheap candidate stays ruled out by construction: `updateTrueScaleFloor` writes `b.mesh.scale` and nothing else, re-confirmed in one pass over every write to a body's position. **Measured, against the prediction.** The float32 step at Pluto's scene coordinate 11.99 is 9.5367e-7 (2^-20), exactly as predicted. The Pluto-Charon SEPARATION is 3.98e-5 scene units = **41.7 ULP** — the predicted "42" is CONFIRMED, and it was quoting the pair separation; Charon's own orbit about the barycentre is 3.52e-5 = **36.9 ULP**. Pluto's radius is 2.41e-6 = **2.5 ULP**, also as predicted. Rebased, that same separation sits where the step is 3.64e-12: **1.09e7 ULP**, confirming "about 1e7". End to end: a vertex on the orbit line beside Pluto is drawn **3.8e-7 scene units** from where it belongs — 1.1% of Charon's whole orbit — and rebased it lands within **2.8e-7 OF** Charon's orbit. Over a slow 600-frame pan the absolute vertex holds only **148 distinct positions** and jumps a full ULP when it moves; that staircase IS the vibration. Rebased it holds 600, moving one camera-step per frame. **Where the notes left a choice — rebuild vs per-object offset — the answer is NEITHER.** An offset is the wrong instrument: it moves the object in float64 but leaves magnitude-12 numbers in the vertex buffer, so both the shape quantisation and the shader cancellation survive it untouched. A full rebuild re-propagates 1024 samples per ring, and for a belt would re-randomise the rubble field (`buildBeltBand` calls `Math.random`) — i.e. it would change how the scene LOOKS. The absolute holders instead keep a float64 MASTER copy of their vertices and re-emit from it: one array pass, the subtraction done in float64 and rounded once. The grid gets the same treatment — its outermost ring sits at rMax, which for Sol is Pluto's own distance, so it is as much a reference line as the orbits are — with its AU labels translated rather than re-made, since they are canvas textures. **Belts are the exception and stay ABSOLUTE.** Their rocks are baked host-relative and the group is re-anchored to the host's rendered position every frame, so they follow the rebase for free; putting them through the rebased choke point would count the origin twice. Moon rings, planetary rings and surface-locked constructs likewise need nothing — all three are placed from a parent's rendered position. **The policy.** Rebase once the camera's target has drifted more than 2000x the working distance from the origin. That multiplier holds the float32 error to 1.5e-4 of the view width (a fifth of a pixel at 1000 px), and it is also what keeps the whole thing invisible at readable scale: there the camera never comes closer than the controls' 0.05 floor, which puts the threshold at 100 scene units against an outermost body at 12 — so the origin never leaves zero and that end of both dials is bit-identical. Suppressed while a focus ease is in flight, so a fly-in re-emits once on arrival instead of on 48 consecutive frames. **What is NOT done.** The on-screen pass. The numbers live in `src/lib/holo/floatingOrigin.spec.ts` (15 assertions) and `npm run build` plus the full suite are green (only E1 fails), but the browser pane in the session that did the work could not composite frames, so nobody has yet LOOKED at Pluto/Charon at 1:1 scale and 1:1 distances, or panned slowly across the outer system. Read A22 before doing that — it explains a second reason the pair may not appear to sit on a line. | fixed v2.1.319-beta |

Giving the drift an out-of-plane velocity means deciding what that deflection does in 3D, which is a transit-physics question. Until then a coasting ship holds the depth it had when it was stranded, which is at least continuous. **BANKED 2026-08-03, EXPLICITLY FOR THE INTERSTELLAR AUTOPILOT WORK.** The data-model gap is real but the case it serves — a ship adrift between stars, replotting from where it sits — only bites once ships routinely fly interstellar routes under their own control. Pick this up as part of that feature, not before; building a 3D interstellar position with nothing flying through it is a schema change in search of a user. **ONE HALF OF IT IS NOT BANKED AND HAS MOVED TO [[A41]]:** a ship shown ON an interstellar route should sit in the correct 3D place along that route. That is a RENDERING question rather than a data-model one — the route's endpoints have z, so a ship's position along it can be interpolated in 3D today without any schema change — and it is the natural companion to A41's work making routes run to the stars rather than to their plane projections. | captured |

The moon rings already solve exactly this: `buildMoonOrbitRing` stores vertices in the parent's local frame and `updateOrbitRings` positions the loop at the parent each frame via `trackParentId`. A barycentre member wants the same, tracked against its barycentre's rendered point. **FIXED v2.1.320-beta, and it was the answer to the reported symptom too.** Each member now gets a ring about its barycentre's rendered point, stored in that point's local frame and tracked to it every frame. The two local-frame builders (moon, member) are now ONE function taking a per-sample radial rule: a ring has to be laid down with exactly the transform the body's own placement uses or the body will not sit on it, and keeping the two rules side by side is what stops them drifting. Barycentres carry a ring but no mesh, so their scene points are now kept alongside the bodies in `updatePositions` — which also means they move with a floating-origin rebase like everything else. Nested pairs fall out for free (no partner radius, so no clearance, so pure physics). | fixed v2.1.320-beta |
| A23 | **An orbit ring is a 1024-gon, and past a certain zoom you are inside one of its facets.** Measured while closing A19/A22, and the reason a framed Pluto appeared to sit off its line even after the floating origin removed the jitter. `ORBIT_SAMPLES` is 1024 for every heliocentric ring whatever its radius, so at Pluto's 12 scene units a single chord sags **5.6e-5 scene units** off the true ellipse — **1.4x the entire Pluto-Charon separation**. It is a RESOLUTION limit, not a precision one: the vertices are exactly right, the straight line between them is not. A22 makes it moot for the pair (their own rings are 3e5 times smaller, where 1024 samples sag 1.6e-10), but it still applies to ANY body zoomed in far enough against its own heliocentric ring — Earth framed at Luna's orbit is the next case up. Options, none costed: raise the sample count globally (4096 brings Pluto's sag to 0.09x the pair separation, at 4x the buffer and 4x the propagation on every `setSystem`, which is already the prime suspect for the random slowdowns); scale the count per ring from its radius; or re-emit the ring non-uniformly around the floating origin on a rebase, which now has somewhere natural to live since the rings already keep a float64 master and are re-emitted there. **FIXED v2.1.321-beta by the THIRD option, and confirmed on screen first — the kink was visible in the outer line beside Pluto.** Diagnosis sharpened: the visible artefact is the 0.35 degree TURN at each vertex, not the sag, because the line spans the whole screen; that is why raising the count cannot win (the kink alone wants ~16k samples at that zoom, and deeper zoom wants more again). The same 1024 samples are now redistributed by a monotonic cubic warp of the orbit parameter, packed into the arc nearest the floating origin. The centre density is SOLVED from the tolerance — chord sag within camDist/2000, sub-pixel at any zoom — rather than picked, so it is correct at 1e-5 and at 1e-2 alike. Costs: the ring to refine is found by scanning the existing float64 master (no propagation), and only a ring passing within 8 camera-distances is refined, so in practice exactly ONE re-propagates per rebase. Re-emitted on rebase and on any zoom past 1.6x, and never called at all while the origin is at zero, so readable scale is untouched. The far side degrades to ~1 degree per vertex at the deepest zooms, which is only ever when it is also 24 scene units away and subtends nothing. **REOPENED AND ACTUALLY FIXED v2.1.322-beta — the v2.1.321 refinement was correct and unreachable.** Its gate asked whether the ring passed within 8 camera-distances of the focus and answered with the distance to the nearest VERTEX of the uniform master. On a 1024-gon at 12 scene units the vertices are 0.074 apart, so a ring passing exactly THROUGH the focus reports 0.037 — **46x over the threshold** — and every ring silently took the uniform path. It now measures the distance to the nearest SEGMENT (the two meeting at that vertex), which is what the question meant; the vertex scan stays, because it fixes the orbit parameter the refinement is centred on. A LESSON worth keeping: a proximity test against a sampled curve must be against its segments, never its samples, or the sampling pitch becomes the floor. Second fault found while proving the first: the dense arc was centred on the floating ORIGIN, which only re-latches after the target has drifted 2000 camera-distances (0.2 scene units at camDist 1e-4) against a dense arc 0.15 wide — so a followed body walked out of its own refinement. The refinement now follows the CAMERA and the rebase follows precision, and it re-emits once the focus crosses a quarter of the arc. | fixed v2.1.322-beta |

With "Live readings" off there is therefore no acceleration or Δv row at all — which is honest, but a catalogue entry for a ship would certainly quote a Δv, and quoting the current one under a capacity heading would be exactly the fault A29 exists to fix. **What is missing is a FULL-TANKS figure:** Δv at `fuelCapacity`, and the acceleration band from full to empty. **Neither would be new physics** — `ConstructDerivedSpecs.svelte` (~:89-92) already derives an accel range across `fuelCapacity_tonnes` for the GM panel, so the arithmetic exists; it is not on `ConstructSpecs`, so the document layer cannot read it without recomputing, and A2's standing rule is that this layer READS derived values rather than deriving its own. **The fix is therefore in `construct-logic.ts`, not in the document:** add rated `deltaV`/`accel` fields to `ConstructSpecs` next to the current ones, then the capacity view can print a rated Δv and the GM panel can stop computing its range inline. Small, but it crosses out of the document layer, which is why A29 stopped short. Related: [[A29]], [[A2]]. **FIXED v2.1.345-beta, in `construct-logic.ts` as the entry directed — not in the document.** `ConstructSpecs` now carries `ratedVacuumDeltaV_ms`, `ratedAccelFullG` and `ratedAccelEmptyG`, computed inside `calculateFullConstructSpecs` beside the current-state pair, so ONE function owns the quantity. With "Live readings" OFF the block prints `Δv (rated, full tanks)` and `Acceleration (rated) — a-b g, full to empty`; with it ON the current `Δv (vacuum)` and `Max acceleration` return, unchanged. The LABEL says which is on show, per A29's own precedent. **THE DECISION WORTH REVIEWING: the rated figures use an EMPTY HOLD, not the current cargo.** Two reasons, and the first is a leak. Capacity mode already prints Dry mass AND Fuel capacity, so a rated Δv computed with the current cargo aboard lets a reader solve straight back to the cargo A29 deliberately withheld — the block would be withholding a reading in one row and handing it over in the next, which is exactly the "quietly wrong" pattern A29 exists to prevent. Second, it is simply what rated MEANS: a property of the ship, not of today's manifest. There is a test that pins it — loading the hold to capacity must not move the rated Δv by a digit. **THE GM PANEL NOW READS THE FIGURE INSTEAD OF COMPUTING IT.** `ConstructDerivedSpecs.svelte` was scaling `maxVacuumG` by mass inline to build its full→empty band; that was a second derivation of what the spec sheet now publishes, and two sums of one quantity drifting apart is precisely how [[B8]] happened. **KNOW THIS BEFORE COMPARING SCREENSHOTS: the GM's band CHANGED MEANING slightly** — it used to carry the current cargo in both ends and is now the ship's rated envelope with an empty hold, so a laden ship's band reads a little higher than before. That is deliberate; a "rated" prefix was added to the panel, and a `Rated Δv (full tanks)` row beside the current one. **A formatting fault surfaced and was fixed with it:** `toFixed(2)` printed the whole band of an ion-drive station as "0.00–0.00 g". Accelerations under 1 g now use two significant figures keyed on the SMALLER end, so the Lunar Gateway reads "0.000048–0.0011 g, full to empty" rather than two zeroes. **Verified live in capacity mode on the holo preset panel and in the full document:** Lunar Gateway shows Acceleration (rated) 0.000048–0.0011 g and Δv (rated, full tanks) 78.5 km/s; the ISS, which has no thrust, correctly shows neither. Two tests added. Related: [[A29]], [[A2]], [[B8]]. **FOLLOW-UP v2.1.346-beta, on direct instruction: the whole construct block was re-gated by ONE rule — a row is a live reading if it changes minute to minute, and a specification if it does not.** **CONFIRMED, not changed: capacity mode already showed `Cargo capacity` and `Fuel capacity` as capacities** — checked on screen and now pinned by a test, because it was the first thing asked about. **`Status` is now live-only.** `flight_state` is literally the ship's state; a reference work does not say where a vessel is this afternoon. **`Location` follows the same rule but only bites when it has to:** a berth — an orbit, a dock, a landing — stays in capacity mode, because a standing assignment is the kind of thing a catalogue lists. A construct UNDER WAY has no berth and its `orbit_string` is telemetry ("Deep Space (v=12.3 km/s)"), so the row is absent rather than quoting a speed under a capacity heading. **`Manifest` (`cargoDescription`) is back, live-only — and this REVERSES a shipped [[A27]] decision, so read it before re-stripping anything.** A27 deleted the prose from `computePlayerSnapshot` outright, reasoning that a star catalogue would not know what is in a hold. That reasoning turned out to be the exact statement the "Live readings" toggle now makes, so the question was a display one after all. The delete is gone from `system/utils.ts` and the row rides beside the cargo TONNAGE it describes. **The consequence is A29's, taken knowingly on the same terms: the prose crosses the wire whatever the preset says.** Do not reinstate the strip without being asked. **`Route` is new, live-only.** A ship's route is a reading of its intent. Only the autopilot PLAN survives to a player — the starmap snapshot strips `scheduled_journeys` and `draft_transit_plan` — so this is the route it flies, not the schedule it flies it on, which is what a watcher could infer anyway. Legs render as verbs with named places ("Mine water ice → Luna (looping)"); `FactContext` gained an optional `system` so a leg can name its target instead of printing an id, and a leg it cannot name is described by its verb rather than dropped. **Ruled out as specifications, so they stay in both modes:** Type, Dimensions, Dry mass, Spin gravity, Power surplus/output, Aerobraking, Orbital period (a property of the orbit, not of the moment), Tags. **NOT SCREEN-VERIFIED, and this is the gap to close: no construct in either bundled map carries a `cargoDescription` OR an autopilot route,** so the Manifest and Route rows are covered by tests with exact expected strings but have not been seen live. To check them: give a construct a cargo description in its Basics tab and a one-leg route in its Autopilot tab, then open a `datapad` or `console` player view. The capacity-side gating (capacities present, Status absent, berth kept) WAS confirmed on screen. Six more tests. | fixed v2.1.345-346-beta |

One added condition. **The reasoning for stopping at nothing rather than substituting a glyph:** the wrong picture is worse than no picture, so removing it is the whole of the reported fault; choosing what a construct SHOULD look like is a design question with real options (the `◆` glyph, the `icon_type`/`icon_color` pair the starmap and holo scene already use, a silhouette by hull class) and inventing one mid-fix is how a look ends up in code instead of in data. | A17 | **THE MEASURE TOOL HAS NEVER COUNTED DEPTH. It reports the planar distance whatever the campaign setting says.** Found by the A15 regression check, NOT caused by it — this predates A8 and A12 and has been wrong since WS7 introduced z on 2026-07-30. **Evidence:** Vega (depth +16 ly) to Zeta Reticuli (depth -35 ly) reads **34.17 ly**, identical with "ignore depth" on and off. The pair is 51 ly apart in depth ALONE, so no 3D separation between them can be below 51; the honest figure is about `sqrt(34.17² + 51²) ≈ 61 ly`. A GM measuring that pair is being told roughly HALF the distance the routes and journey durations for the same pair would use. **Root cause, and it is not where you would look.** The plumbing is right: `measureDist` (`Starmap.svelte:692`) already calls `systemSeparation(mA, mB, pixelsPerUnit, !zCounts(starmap))`, so the flag is wired correctly and the 3D branch does run. The endpoints are what is wrong — `measurePick(x, y, label, constructId)` (`:673`) takes only x and y, and the call site passes `s.position.x, s.position.y` (`:704`), dropping `s.position.z`. `posZ()` then reads both endpoints' absent z as 0, so the "3D" calculation returns the planar answer and the flag can change nothing. This is why the setting appears to work everywhere else: routes and journeys pass whole `position` objects. **Fix is small but not one line, and it needs its own verification:** add z to `MeasureEnd`, pass `s.position.z` at `:704`, and carry z through `resolveMeasure` (`:681`) for construct endpoints — which means `constructDisplayPlacement` has to supply a z for transit/adrift points too, or ship measurements stay planar while system measurements go 3D, which would be worse than the honest bug. Deliberately NOT fixed inside the A15 check: changing what a measurement REPORTS changes what the campaign counts, so it wants its own commit and its own before/after. **FIXED v2.1.314-beta. Four numbers, same pair, both zooms: depth counting 60.99 / 60.99 ly, depth ignored 34.17 / 34.17 ly.** The arithmetic checks out independently — `60.99² − 34.17² = 2552`, so Δz ≈ 50.5, which is what the two labels round to at ±1 (they print 16 and −35 via `Math.round`). **What was ruled out:** the flag, the predicate and the module were all innocent. `measureDist` already passed `!zCounts(starmap)`, `systemSeparation`'s 3D branch always ran, and `posZ` did exactly what it documents. The coordinate was amputated one level above all of them, at the pick. **The second caller, decided:** a CONSTRUCT endpoint needs no z at pick time, because `resolveMeasure` re-derives its whole position from the clock every frame — anything stored at the pick is overwritten immediately. So the ship's depth had to come from the placement instead, and `ConstructPlacement` now carries it wherever it is EXACTLY derivable: resting in a system it is that system's z; in transit it is the same lerp as x and y, because an interstellar hop is a straight line and `frac` was already on the placement. **Two honest gaps left, deliberately, and both are data-model not display:** a POINT origin/destination (`fromX/fromY`, `toX/toY`) has no `fromZ/toZ` in the journey schema, and `AdriftConstruct` stores only x/y — so a ship stranded in interstellar space has no recorded depth and reads as being on the plane. Also NOT invented: a `vz` for a coasting drift, because the slingshot deflection is modelled as a planar rotation of `vx/vy` and giving it an out-of-plane component is a transit-physics decision, not a display one. A coasting ship holds the depth it had when stranded. See A21. **Pinned by a test at the level the bug lived** (`Starmap.spec.ts`, "measure tool depth (A17)"): it drives the real path — ruler on, tap two stars, read the label — on a fixture 40 apart in plan and 9 in depth, so the answers are exactly 41 and 40. A unit test of `systemSeparation` would NOT have caught this, since that module was never wrong; confirmed by reverting the call site, which fails the test with `expected '40 ly' to be '41 ly'`. | fixed v2.1.314-beta |
| A14 | **What should the 3D starmap do when the campaign ignores depth?** Raised by A12, deliberately left unanswered there. A12 drops the depth cues from the 2D GM starmap on the grounds that annotating a number which affects no distance is noise. The same argument does not obviously carry to the 3D view, because in 3D the depth is not an annotation — it is the geometry, and the whole reason for the view. Three coherent answers: (a) leave it, and treat "ignore depth" as a MEASUREMENT setting only, which is exactly what `systemDistance.ts` says it is ("`ignoreZ` is the campaign's own choice… so an existing map keeps the distances it always had") — the 3D view then honestly shows a layout whose separations are not what the campaign counts; (b) flatten the 3D view to the plane when the flag is on, which makes the two views agree but throws away the placement work and arguably makes the 3D view pointless for that campaign; (c) keep the geometry but suppress the numeric read-outs, the same line A12 drew in 2D. Not a bug; a decision about what the setting means. Worth deciding before someone "fixes" the 3D view to match the 2D one. **DECIDED 2026-07-31: option (c).** Keep the geometry — bodies stay where they were placed, because that is the entire point of the 3D view — and suppress the numeric depth READ-OUTS, which is exactly the line A12 drew in 2D. The reasoning is then consistent across both views: the placement is real and stays visible, the number that affects no distance is not asserted. Option (b) is explicitly rejected: flattening throws away placement work. Implement via `zCounts()` (`src/lib/map/systemDistance.ts:22`), never by reading the flag directly. **BUILT 2026-07-31 at v2.1.312 — and the decision turned out to need NO behaviour change, which is a result rather than a dodge.** Both halves of option (c) were already true, and this is a proof rather than a sample. **Geometry is kept:** `Starmap3DView.svelte:53` passes `z` through unconditionally, and nothing in the 3D path can do otherwise — `src/lib/starmap/**` and the catalogue route never import `systemDistance`, never call `zCounts()` and never reference `ignoreZForDistances`; the single mention in `starmapScene.ts:201` is a comment saying distances live elsewhere. The flag cannot reach the scene, so option (b) was never a risk here. **There is no numeric depth read-out to suppress:** the scene draws exactly three kinds of text — system name (`starmapScene.ts:586`), route name (`:603`) and the grid distance rings (`:384`), and the rings come from `spanMap = max(maxX-minX, maxY-minY)` (`:532`), which is planar and never sees z. A search of the whole tree for a signed depth figure finds exactly two, both the 2D GM cues A12 already handles; `position.z` has only three consumers in `src/` (`Starmap.svelte`, `map/rebase.ts`, `map/systemDistance.ts`), so no document, panel or player surface prints a depth anywhere. **NO `zCounts()` call was added, deliberately:** a guard on a read-out that does not exist would be dead code asserting a rule it does not enforce. What WAS added is the durable part — a comment at the `z` pass-through recording the A14 decision and its reasoning, at the one line where a future session could break it by "making 3D match 2D". Note also that there is no GM 3D starmap at all: `Starmap3DView` is mounted only by the player catalogue and the preset-editor preview. | verified v2.1.312-beta |

Being unified into shared components — `FloatGrip.svelte`, `FloatPin.svelte` and a new `src/lib/ui/` — with `TimeControls.svelte` losing the bulk of its own implementation and `BodyPicker.svelte` adopting the shared one. The player catalogue has its own separate, much smaller time puck (`.time-controls` at `catalogue/+page.svelte:1068`: a play/pause button, a rate slider and `use:clickOutside`), which this change did not touch and which still works. The player surface IS reached by this batch, but through `BodyPicker`, not `TimeControls` — so the A11 trap is real and the verification still had to happen, just on the picker. **Verification done on every surface (2026-07-31, at v2.1.312).** GM starmap: both controls, drag / lock / auto-close / open-rightwards. GM SYSTEM view (the mount that had not been exercised): unlock puts the pill away to its clock, dragging the clock moves it 180/-60 without counting as the tap that opens it, tapping reopens with the grip back and wholly on screen, and touching the orrery canvas closes it again. The floating control models a puck that hides itself and remembers a POSITION; the info panel is a persistent notes panel that remembers a position AND A SIZE (A13), anchors by absolute `left/top` rather than an offset from a host anchor, is dragged by its whole header rather than a grip, and must NOT auto-close — auto-hiding notes you are typing into would be a bug. | A15 | **Regression check: does the MEASURE TOOL still work after A8 and A12?** Raised while deciding A14, not a reported fault — a check that has to be done before the batch is trusted. Both changes touched it from different directions. A8 (v2.1.310) made the measure read-out hold a constant screen size under zoom, so it now divides by `labelK` like the other labels — a read-out that renders at the wrong size, in the wrong place, or not at all would be that change. A12 (v2.1.309) hides depth cues when the campaign ignores depth, and the measure tool is precisely where depth is meant to STOP counting rather than stop being shown: `zCounts()` governs whether a measured distance is planar or 3D, and A12 must not have altered the arithmetic — only the annotation. **Verify both readings:** measure between two systems with the flag OFF (depth counts, the figure should be the 3D separation) and ON (planar), at more than one zoom level, and confirm the read-out is legible and correctly placed at each. If the figure moved when only the ANNOTATION should have, that is a real bug in A12 and it is more serious than anything A12 fixed. **DONE 2026-07-31 at v2.1.312. The depth ANNOTATIONS behaved: 41 cues → 0 → 41 across the toggle, with the measure read-out unaffected throughout. **But the figure not moving is itself the finding.** It should have moved, and 34.17 ly is impossible for that pair: the two systems are 51 ly apart in depth alone, so no 3D separation between them can be less than 51. The tool has never counted depth — see A17. Neither A8 nor A12 caused it: `measurePick` and its call site last changed on 2026-06-16 (`f626123`, `f5c6e72`), before WS7 added z at all, and neither of this batch's commits touches them. | verified v2.1.312-beta |
| A32 | **Changing the info-panel width does not take effect unless the player window is ALREADY OPEN when you save — and the top third of the slider does nothing at all.** Reported 2026-08-01: "it ONLY updates if I have the window open already and edit and save it — maybe it is scaling of old window rather than current size". The instinct is right, and there are THREE faults in five lines, only one of which was reported. **VERIFIED, all in `src/routes/catalogue/+page.svelte`.** **(1) THE CONVERSION IS ONE-SHOT.** `applyPlayerPreset(p)` (`:350`) converts the stored fraction to pixels at `:357` — `inspectorWidth = Math.max(200, Math.min(640, Math.round(p.inspectorWidthPct * window.innerWidth)))` — and that is the ONLY place it happens. It is never recomputed on resize, so the pixel width is frozen against whatever the viewport was when the preset was last applied. That is precisely why editing and saving with the window open works: it re-runs `applyPlayerPreset` against the current size. A window opened later, or resized after, keeps a stale figure. **(2) THE CLAMP KILLS THE TOP OF THE SLIDER, and this is [[F10]] RECURRING IN MIRROR IMAGE.** The slider's range is 0.15 to 0.50 (`PlayerPresetEditor.svelte:541`) but the live view clamps to `min(640, ...)`. On a 1920 px display 50% is 960 px, clamped to 640 px = 33%, so roughly the top third of the travel moves nothing. F10 fixed exactly this fault in the PREVIEW, which was drawing a raw pixel figure capped at 340 — nobody checked the LIVE view, which caps at 640. Whatever is decided, the editor's range and the live clamp must agree, or the slider is lying again. **(3) TWO SOURCES OF TRUTH FOR ONE NUMBER.** `inspectorWidth` is ALSO seeded from `localStorage['holo-insp-width']` (`:186-187`) and written by the drag handle (`:191-196`) as a PIXEL value, while the preset stores a FRACTION. Last writer wins and the two do not mean the same thing — a width dragged on one screen is a different proportion on another, which is the very problem F10 moved to fractions to solve. Decide which owns the value; the F10 reasoning says the FRACTION should, with the drag writing back a fraction rather than pixels. **The proper fix makes the pixel width a DERIVED, REACTIVE quantity** — a function of the stored fraction and the CURRENT viewport, recomputed on resize — rather than a variable assigned once at apply time. Related: [[F10]], [[A13]]. **FIXED v2.1.342-beta — all three, plus a fourth the verification turned up, and there was a FIFTH mechanism nobody had named.** Root cause exactly as scoped for (1)(2)(3), and the proper fix was taken: `inspectorWidth` is now a REACTIVE DERIVATION of a stored fraction and the live viewport (`$: inspectorWidth = clamp(pct × viewportW)`), with `<svelte:window bind:innerWidth>` feeding it, so it is right on a window opened later and tracks a resize. **THE FIFTH MECHANISM, and it is the one worth reading: making it reactive was not enough, because SVELTE ORDERS `$:` STATEMENTS BY THE ASSIGNMENTS IT CAN SEE.** `applyPlayerPreset` is called FROM a reactive block, so a write to `inspectorWidthPct` buried inside that function cannot order the derivation that reads it — the derivation had already run for that cycle and was never marked dirty again. Measured live: the panel sat at the local default (342 px = 0.18 × 1898) while the preset asked for 0.26, i.e. the preset's width reached nothing at all. The adoption therefore happens IN the reactive block, in plain sight, with a comment saying why it must stay there. This is A32's own fault — a one-way write nobody re-reads — in a second costume, and it would have shipped looking fixed. **(2) The clamp is gone and the ranges agree:** bounds are `INSP_MIN_PCT`/`INSP_MAX_PCT` = 0.15/0.50, character-for-character the editor's slider range, with a 200 px readability floor that is itself capped at half the viewport so it can never exceed the maximum on a narrow screen. Confirmed at the top of the travel: 50% on an 1898 px display gives **949 px**, where the old `min(640, ...)` gave 640 (34%). **(3) DECIDED: the FRACTION owns the value, and the drag writes a fraction.** New key `holo-insp-width-pct` (the old `holo-insp-width` pixel key is abandoned, not migrated — beta). **The tie-break needed one more distinction than the triage names, and this is the judgement call to review:** a stored drag wins on the FIRST application in a window, so a width the reader dragged survives a reload; every LATER application — the GM editing or swapping the preset live — wins over it, because that is what deploying a preset is for. Preset-always-wins would have meant a dragged width never surviving a reload; drag-always-wins would have meant a GM could never set it. **(4) FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, fixed in the same commit: the drag handle was `display: none` at every width.** `.insp-resize { display: none }` sits AFTER the `@media (min-width: 720px)` rule that un-hides it, at equal specificity, so the later rule won everywhere — the panel edge could not be dragged at all. Now `.inspector .insp-resize`. Without it fault (3) has no way to be exercised, which is presumably why it went unnoticed. **Verified live on a 1898 px display, GM + player window side by side, every case:** width changed with the player window SHUT then opened → 949 px (50%); resize → tracks (1500 → 390 px = 26%, 760 → 200 px floor); drag → stores `0.3462` (a proportion, not pixels) and reload restores 759 px = 40%; GM edits the preset to 20% with the window OPEN → 380 px, so the deploy still lands. Note the harness caveat for the next session: a CDP viewport override does NOT emit a `resize` event, so the resize case has to be driven by dispatching one. **RULED OUT:** nothing was changed in `PlayerPresetEditor` — its slider and preview were already right after F10, and the live view was the only side that disagreed. Related: [[F10]], [[A13]]. | fixed v2.1.342-beta |
| A33 | **Two differently-scaled radiation numbers with similar names sit near each other, and the small one reads as a bug.** Reported 2026-08-01 as "radiation is super high on Io but lowish on Mars". **Mars is not low — it is very nearly exact.** `surfaceRadiation` for Mars is **213.69 mSv/yr** against the ~210 mSv/yr Curiosity's RAD instrument measures on the martian surface, i.e. within about 2%. The figure that looks wrong is `irradiationDose: 0.574`, which is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY — `radiation.ts:8` describes it as the cumulative high-energy dose a surface has taken, RELATIVE, with Earth-unshielded-young about 1. It is a surface-ageing ratio, not an annual dose, and it has no business being read on the same scale as a mSv/yr figure. **The rest of the column is right too, which is why the pairing is the fault rather than the physics:** Earth 2.30 mSv/yr against ~2.4 background, Venus 2.0 under 92 bar, Mercury 3,500 unshielded and close in, Phobos 223.9 consistent with Mars beside it. **This is the same fault as [[A5]]** — two numbers describing related but different things, adjacent, with nothing in the presentation to say they are on different scales. A5 was a mean sitting outside its own range; this is a ratio sitting beside a dose. Fix it the same way: make the block say what each number IS. Options are to label the units explicitly, to move the relative figure away from the absolute one, or to drop `irradiationDose` from the reader-facing block entirely if its only real consumer is the ageing model. **Check what else in that block is a ratio rather than a measurement while you are there** — the A5 sweep found [[B8]] by doing exactly that. Related: [[A5]], [[B8]], [[B20]]. **FIXED v2.1.344-beta as a LABELLING change. NEITHER NUMBER WAS TOUCHED, and the triage's premise turned out to be half wrong in a way that matters.** **`irradiationDose` IS NOT IN THE READER-FACING BLOCK AT ALL, and never was** — checked before removing anything, as the entry asked. Its only consumers are `planetAppearance.ts` (tholins and regolith greying) and the GM's physics trace. So there was nothing to drop. **What the reader actually sees of it is its BUCKET, as the `surface/irradiation` tag, in the same block as the dose rows, under the label "Irradiation".** That is the fault the report describes, one layer down from where it was looked for. **Io is the proof the two are different quantities:** constantly resurfaced, so its `irradiationDose` is 0.000 and the tag reads LOW, printed inches from a surface-radiation row of 36 Sv/DAY. **DECIDED: rename the label to "Space weathering"** (the tag KEY `surface/irradiation` is untouched — it is serialised) and say in its description that it is a cumulative total relative to a young unshielded Earth, not a dose per year, so it does not compare with the rows above. **THE SWEEP FOUND TWO MORE, and the first is worse than the reported one.** **(a) The radiation rows themselves were on two scales, side by side.** The mean-only path auto-scaled to Sv/y or Sv/day, but the range path printed raw mSv/y whatever the magnitude AND SHOWED NO MEAN — so Earth read "high (229.6–229.6 mSv/y)" on one line and "high (843 Sv/y)" on the next: two doses a thousandfold apart, told apart by a suffix on one of them, with no absolute figure on the first row. Io's range came out as an eight-digit millisievert figure. Now one helper picks the unit ONCE from the mean, prints the mean WITH that unit, and prints the range in the same unit and precision — Mars "high · 214 mSv/y (178–258)", Io "high · 36 Sv/day (35–37)", Earth "high · 230 mSv/y" (a range whose ends round alike is suppressed rather than printed as "230–230"). **(b) An INDEX printed as a percentage one row above a real coverage percentage:** "Habitability 83%" against "Native life present (cover 80%)", with nothing to say the first was a score rather than a fraction of the surface. A square line runs the full width at some z, so its endpoints sit at a distance of at least 28.8 - beyond 22.8 - and `addLattice` drops any segment whose both ends have faded out. 'grid' : gridMode` translated correctly, so the square branch was being reached every time. Also closed in passing: the else-branch drew hexes for ANY non-square type, including `none`. **2b - AND THE GEOMETRY IS NOW ONE GENERATOR: `src/lib/map/latticeGeometry.ts`.** Square and hex, in map space, unit-agnostic, with `travellerHexLabel` and `hexCentres` alongside so a label can never sit in a hex the lattice did not draw. It takes a `maxSegment` option documented with the reason it exists: a caller that fades per vertex MUST segment, or it judges a whole line by its far ends. **Proved numerically rather than looked at** - `latticeGeometry.spec.ts` asserts that an unsegmented square lattice has ZERO edges surviving the real fade radius and a segmented one has many, with hex unaffected either way. Seven tests. **HEX AND TRAVELLER-HEX RENDER UNCHANGED, and that took care:** squares take the THINNED cell (drawn per grid line, so a dense map can be skipped through) while hexes keep the true cell, because thinning a hex lattice moves the centres a system is snapped to. The density bail and the label offset are preserved deliberately. **2c - THE PREMISE OF THE 2D HALF IS WRONG, AND CHECKING IT WAS THE WHOLE OF THAT STAGE. `Starmap2DView.svelte` has no grid handling because NOTHING MOUNTS IT.** It is imported once, in `catalogue/+page.svelte`, and rendered nowhere. **The player's 2D starmap is `Starmap3DView` with `flat` set** - the same renderer locked overhead at `angleDeg` 0 - and the page says so in as many words at `:1021`: "3D (or 2D = the same renderer LOCKED OVERHEAD)". `flat` pins the tilt and re-runs `setData`; it does not touch `rebuildGrid`. **So the two views are not two implementations agreeing by luck, they are ONE implementation, and 2b fixed both at once** - a stronger parity than the item asked for. Adding grid styles to `Starmap2DView` would have been work that could never appear on screen, which is the trap this very item warned about one level up. Dead import removed, component annotated so the next reader is not misled the same way; NOT deleted, because whether it is a discarded prototype or an intended lighter renderer is not this session's call. Recorded unnumbered. **THE HOOK FOR [[G4]], since 2a left an obvious one and the brief asked me to say so:** every G4 feature is now a property of ONE generator rather than three. Brightness falloff already exists as `addLattice`'s `fadeFrom`/`fadeTo` and is the mechanism this bug turned on - it just needs exposing. Thicker subsector edges want a per-edge WEIGHT on `LatticeEdge`, which is one field on the returned tuple. Hex numbering is already factored out as `travellerHexLabel` + `hexCentres`. And "the 3D hex look for all types" is now literally a matter of routing `square` through the same styling as `hex`, since both come from one function. **NOT BUILT - G4 remains open.** **SEEN ON SCREEN 2026-08-02, AND THREE THINGS CAME BACK - all fixed at v2.1.373-beta.** **(1) Traveller hex was indistinguishable from plain hex.** Two causes, and the second is the one that mattered. The numbering gate was `hd >= 0.5` SCENE units, and with GRID_RADIUS 12 that means a hex has to be about a twenty-fourth of the whole field before a number appears - above a typical bundled map, so the numbers simply never drew. Lowered to 0.22: still a legibility gate, set where a number is readable rather than where it is comfortable. **But numbering alone was never going to be enough, because it only shows when the hexes are large.** What makes a Traveller map READ as one at any zoom is the SUBSECTOR GRID, and that did not exist in the 3D renderer at all - only in the GM's 2D `Grid.svelte`. | A38 | **The 3D body graphic in the DOCUMENT ignores the view filter — a plain white sphere on a green CRT page.** Reported 2026-08-02 with a screenshot of Epsilon Eridani III in the console/CRT preset: every glyph is green phosphor with scanlines and noise, and the body renders as an unfiltered white low-poly globe sitting on top of it. **The mechanism is visible in the code's own reasoning.** `catalogue/document/bodyImage.ts:3-4` restricts photos to same-origin URLs because "a cross-origin image would taint **the WebGL surface the filter reads from**" — so the document is drawn into a canvas which WebGL then filters, and ANYTHING DRAWN INTO THAT CANVAS IS FILTERED BY CONSTRUCTION. The sphere is not, which points at it being rendered SEPARATELY and composited OVER the filtered result rather than into it. Confirm that before fixing: find where the `bodyDisc` block in `mode: 'sphere'` is actually produced and whether its output joins the document canvas or is layered above it. **THE FIX IS TO GET IT INSIDE THE PASS, NOT TO RE-TINT IT.** Do not approximate the filter on the sphere with a CSS filter or a colour multiply — that is a second implementation of the filter which will drift from the real one, and the preview-versus-live drift that shared resolvers exist to prevent has already bitten in [[F9]]. **ALSO REQUESTED: CHECK THE OTHER MODES DO RESPECT IT.** Photo, simple disc and flat shape are all 2D draws into the document canvas and should therefore be filtered already — verify rather than assume, and say which you checked. Note the side PANEL takes a different route from the full document: `catalogue/+page.svelte:903` applies `cssFilterApprox(...)` as a CSS `filter` on the `.inspector` aside plus tint and scanline overlay divs (`:904-906`), i.e. an APPROXIMATION, while the full `FilteredDocumentView` uses the real shader. So a body graphic may be filtered on one surface and not the other, and both need checking — that pair has produced two separate faults already ([[F7]], [[F9]]). Related: [[F9]], [[A30]]. **FIXED v2.1.367-beta, and the item's assumption about the other modes was WRONG - which is why it was right to ask.** **Mechanism confirmed before touching anything, exactly where the item predicted.** renderDocument.ts:292 (case 'bodyDisc') reserves a TRANSPARENT GAP and says so in its own comment: "It is NOT drawn into the filtered canvas - the caller overlays the REAL renderer here". FilteredDocumentView then positions BodyGraphic as an absolutely-placed SIBLING of the filtered canvas (.fd-bodygfx), so it was composited over the filtered result and never saw the shader. **THE OTHER MODES, checked rather than assumed, and the answer splits three ways.** **PHOTO is genuinely inside the pass** - it is drawn into the canvas as an image block, and bodyImage.ts's same-origin restriction exists precisely because WebGL reads that canvas. **SPHERE, FLAT and SIMPLE-DISC are ALL overlays**, not just the sphere. Flat and disc merely LOOKED right because BodyGraphic already receives the document's mono/theme colours and the page background, so they were tinted to match without ever being filtered - no scanlines, no barrel warp, no noise on any of them. The reporter noticed the sphere only because a 3D render with its own portrait lighting comes out white instead of ink-coloured. **THE FIX GETS THEM INSIDE THE PASS, and re-tints nothing.** holo/scene.ts gains preserveDrawingBuffer: true - without it a WebGL canvas captured outside its own render callback comes back blank; BodyGraphic exposes getCanvas(); and FilteredDocumentView composites document + graphic into the texture the filter reads, EVERY FRAME, because the body spins and a single upload would freeze it mid-turn. The DOM copy stays mounted at opacity 0 - still rendering, still hit-testable, so drag-to-spin survives - which is the same trick the holo HUD card already uses to keep the inspector's buttons while the shader draws the card. **NOT CAPTURED, and recorded rather than bodged: the SIMPLE-DISC mode is an inline SVG with no canvas to capture**, so it keeps the overlay. A CSS filter on it would be a second implementation of the shader, which is exactly the [[F9]] failure this item warns against. **BOTH SURFACES:** the full document (FilteredDocumentView) is fixed. The side PANEL takes the other route entirely and is unchanged - see [[A39]], which establishes that its canvas is CSS-approximated along with its chrome on the non-holo tiers, and takes the REAL shader on the holo tier via the HUD card. **NOT VERIFIED ON SCREEN - see the handback list.** The Browser pane does not composite in this environment, so requestAnimationFrame never fires, and a per-frame capture is precisely what cannot be tested without compositing. The strongest available evidence is internal precedent: filteredCanvas.ts:24 already relies on the same preserveDrawingBuffer capture, deliberately and with a comment, so the technique is already in production in this repo. | fixed v2.1.367-beta, confirmed by owner 2026-08-07 ("works fine") |
| A39 | **Does the info panel still need the CSS filter approximation now that its content is a canvas?** Asked 2026-08-02 while scoping [[A38]] — "nothing should be using the CSS approximation any more, are they?" **The answer is no, it is not obsolete, but the question lands on something real.** `player/cssFilterApprox.ts:1-4` states its purpose: a CSS approximation of the GPU filters for DOM-RENDERED surfaces, driven by the SAME `filterParams` as the shaders so one preset reads consistently, and explicitly not pixel-identical (barrel warp and the signal-artifact effects have no cheap CSS analogue and are skipped). That is legitimate and not debt: a shader can only filter what is rendered into a texture, and DOM chrome cannot go through GLSL without a capture step. It is also ONE source of truth rendered two ways rather than a rival implementation, which is what distinguishes it from the [[F9]] failure. **Two things in it ARE worth chasing.** (1) The comment marks cover and starmap as INTERIM, "until their true-GLSL capture path lands" — that path has not landed and nothing tracks it. (2) **The better question: the INFO PANEL is listed as a DOM surface, but since D6 unified the info panels onto the document engine, `DocPanel` renders its content to a CANVAS.** `catalogue/+page.svelte:607` and `:903` still apply `cssFilterApprox` to the wrapping `.inspector` aside with tint and scanline overlay divs at `:904-906`, i.e. treating the whole thing as DOM. If its interior is now a canvas, it may be able to take the REAL shader and stop approximating — which would also close the panel-versus-document split that has produced [[F7]], [[F9]] and now [[A38]]. Establish what is actually DOM in that aside (chrome and controls, presumably) versus what is canvas, and whether the two can be filtered separately. **Do this WITH or BEFORE [[A38]]** — both are about which surfaces reach the real filter pass, and answering them separately risks two different answers. Related: [[A38]], [[F9]], [[F7]]. **ANSWERED v2.1.367-beta. NO, IT IS NOT OBSOLETE - AND THE REAL-SHADER PATH FOR THE PANEL ALREADY EXISTS, GATED.** **What is actually in that aside, established rather than assumed:** DOM chrome (the title button, the resize handle, the action buttons) AND a canvas - DocPanel renders the whole document body to one canvas (DocPanel.svelte:132), and it carries no filter of its own. The CSS filter on the .inspector aside therefore covers both, which is why the approximation works and why it cannot simply be deleted: a shader can only wreck what is in a texture, and the chrome is not. **But the panel interior CAN take the real shader, and on one tier it already does.** catalogue/+page.svelte:644 computes hudCardOn = effectiveSystemTier === 'holo' && selectedBody && presetFilterActive && hudW >= 720 && !hideInfoPanel, and when it is true the card is drawn to a canvas and composited into the holo render as a HUD quad - the REAL GLSL - while inspFx is bypassed (!hudCardOn guards the filter, the tint div and the scanline div) and the DOM inspector is kept underneath, invisible, purely for its buttons. So the pattern is built, proven and shipping; what is missing is the same route on the NON-holo tiers (text-list / 2D), where DocPanel's canvas is still CSS-approximated along with its chrome. **That is the honest state, and it is not debt in the way the question implied:** one source of truth (filterParams) rendered two ways, with a real-shader path already taken wherever the surface can support it. **Extending it to the other tiers is real work, deliberately not started here** - it needs a compositing target on tiers that have no holo render to composite into. **The INTERIM note is now tracked rather than orphaned:** cssFilterApprox.ts marks cover and starmap as interim "until their true-GLSL capture path lands". That path has not landed; recorded as an unnumbered capture at the bottom so it stops being a comment nobody owns. | answered v2.1.367-beta - approximation justified, real path exists on the holo tier, extension scoped not built |
| A40 | **"Info text size" in the player preset editor stops at 160% — take it to 250%.** Requested 2026-08-02. **The change itself is one character:** `PlayerPresetEditor.svelte:622` reads `<input type="range" min="0.8" max="1.6" step="0.05" bind:value={draft.infoFontScale} />`. **What actually needs checking is what happens at 2.5x**, because `infoFontScale` reaches several surfaces and one of them may not survive it: the preview panel sizes its base font from it (`:749`), the document engine takes it as `fontScale` (`:752`, `:771`), and the starmap falls back to it when `starmapFontScale` is unset (`:728`). At two and a half times, a heading may no longer fit the panel width, a document block may overflow its measured height, and the starmap labels — which A4 and A8 spent two items making hold a constant screen size — may collide. Raise the cap, then LOOK at each of those four surfaces at the new maximum before calling it done; if something breaks it is likely to be a layout that assumed a bounded scale rather than the scale itself. **Related and worth doing in the same pass: [[A32]] found the identical fault in the WIDTH slider** — the editor's range was 0.15-0.50 while the live view clamped to 640 px, so the top third of the travel did nothing. Check that this slider's full new range actually reaches the live view rather than being re-clamped somewhere downstream, because that is the same trap one control along. **FIXED v2.1.369-beta, AND THE A32 TRAP WAS PRESENT.** `renderDocument.ts:56` clamped `fontScale` to **1.8**, and that is the single choke point between this control and every surface the item lists - the preview panel, the document engine on both stages, and the starmap document. Raising the slider alone would have moved the panel's CSS base font while the document inside it stopped at 180%: the two scaling APART, which reads worse than a capped control. Both ends now say 2.5, with the clamp commented to say it must track the control. **RULED OUT: the 3D starmap LABELS are not on this dial at all.** A4 and A8 made them hold a constant screen size through `labelSize`; the starmap surface that takes `fontScale` is the starmap DOCUMENT, which goes through `renderDocument` like the other three. So all four surfaces share one clamp and there was no second place to raise - the collision risk the item worried about does not exist on this control. **The test is pinned AT the old ceiling, deliberately.** Comparing 2.5 against 1.6 PASSES even with a clamp at 1.8, because 1.8 is still larger - the first version of this test did exactly that and caught nothing. Comparing against 1.8 is the assertion, and reverting the clamp gives 61 against 61 and fails. | fixed v2.1.369-beta |
| A41 | **Routes on the 3D starmap run to a system's PROJECTION on the grid plane, not to the star itself.** Reported 2026-08-03: they should be direct lines to the star position. **THIS IS NOT A DROPPED COORDINATE — IT IS STATED DESIGN THAT PREDATES DEPTH.** `starmap/starmapScene.ts:3` says so in the file's own header: "Routes are lines on the plane." That was correct before WS7 gave systems a z; nobody revisited it afterwards, so the routes are honestly implementing an assumption that stopped being true on 2026-07-30. Related in shape to [[A17]] (the measure tool losing z at the pick) but different in cause: A17 intended 3D and lost the coordinate, this never intended it. **TWO THINGS A WORKER WILL GET WRONG IF THEY TREAT IT AS A ONE-LINER.** (1) **THE GLOW GEOMETRY IS FLAT BY CONSTRUCTION.** The route glow (~`:690`) builds a quad from `dx`/`dz` alone and orients it with `quad.rotation.y = -Math.atan2(dz, dx)` — a yaw-only rotation in the ground plane. A quad that can only yaw cannot follow a line with height. Feeding 3D endpoints to the core `LineSegments` (`:698`) fixes the line and leaves the glow lying flat under it. The glow needs a real 3D orientation, or a different primitive. (2) **IT MUST USE THE EXAGGERATED Z, NOT THE RAW Z.** `Starmap3DView` carries a live `zExaggeration` prop and stars are drawn at exaggerated depth. A route drawn from raw z will MISS the stars at both ends whenever exaggeration is not 1, which is most of the time. Take the same position the star sprite is placed at, do not recompute it — that is the [[A17]] lesson exactly. **Check the route NAME too:** `:671` places it "at the midpoint", and a midpoint computed in the plane will float off the line once the line has height. **Then check the 2D starmap agrees** — depth is presentational there (2D is the plan view, per WS7's standing rule), so routes SHOULD stay planar in 2D and the two views will legitimately differ. Say that explicitly in the entry so nobody later "fixes" the 2D one to match. **ROUTING: `starmapScene.ts` is the file [[A37]] is working in right now** — this is the same file and a natural add-on if that session has room, but it is a distinct change and wants its own commit. **FIXED v2.1.381-beta, and both traps were real.** **The endpoints:** an endpoint is now the system's `center` STRAIGHT OUT OF the `centers` map — the very `Vector3` the star sprite copied its position from — with a constant `LIFT` of 0.02 added as an OFFSET rather than a `.setY(0.02)` that flattened it. Nothing is recomputed from raw z, so the A17 failure is not merely avoided but structurally impossible: there is no second derivation to disagree. **The glow band needed a full basis, exactly as predicted.** `quad.rotation.y = -atan2(dz, dx)` is a yaw and a yaw cannot leave the ground plane, so 3D endpoints on the core line alone would have left the halo on the floor under a sloped line. It is now oriented by `makeBasis(dir, nrm, side)` with local X along the route and local Y (the quad normal) the part of world-up perpendicular to the route — the band is as face-up as a sloped line permits, degenerates safely for a near-vertical route, and is EXACTLY the old flat quad when the route is horizontal. `len` is the true 3D length; `hypot(dx, dz)` was the length of the SHADOW and fell short of the star at both ends independently of the height error. The 0.005 separation that keeps the halo under the core line is now taken along the normal rather than in world y, or a steep route's halo and line would land in one plane and z-fight. The route NAME takes the real midpoint of the real line. **VERIFIED BY DRIVING THE REAL MODULE IN THE BROWSER, not by reproducing it.** The pane does not composite here (screenshots time out, as usual for a worker session), so instead `starmapScene.ts` was imported live from the dev server, `Object3D.prototype.add` patched to capture everything the scene emits, and a synthetic three-system map fed through `createStarmapScene` at three exaggerations. **At 0.5x, 1x and 3x every route endpoint equals its star sprite's position exactly in x and z and by exactly the 0.02 lift in y** — e.g. at 3x the star sits at y 26.496 and the route ends at 26.516, at 0.5x 4.416 and 4.436. The glow quad's local +X came back as the normalised 3D route direction and its length as the 3D length (23.781 at 1x, 34.490 at 3x, against a flat 22.08), and its normal tilts further off vertical as the exaggeration rises — so the band follows the line rather than lying under it. **The 2D plan view is byte-identical to before:** with `flatOverhead` set, every segment is at y 0.02, the quad normal comes back as exactly `(0, 1, 0)`, the quad at y 0.015 and the length 22.08 — the pre-A41 numbers. That path has no special case in the new code; it falls out because `flatMode` zeroes the exaggeration, which is the honest way for it to happen. **THE 2D STARMAP SHOULD STAY PLANAR AND THIS IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT.** 2D is the plan view by WS7's standing rule, so the two views legitimately differ and nobody should later "fix" 2D to match. Note also that the player's "2D starmap" is not `Starmap2DView.svelte` (which nothing mounts, per [[A37]]) — it is this same scene with `flat` set, so the planar behaviour is this file's, verified above. **STILL WANTS A HUMAN EYE, and it is an aesthetic call rather than a correctness one:** the halo is now edge-on to the viewer for a steep route, so a strongly exaggerated map may show thinner glow on its steepest links. Open a map with depth, push the exaggeration slider up, and say whether the band reads well or wants to billboard toward the camera instead. **SCOPE ADDED 2026-08-03: A SHIP SHOWN ON AN INTERSTELLAR ROUTE MUST SIT IN THE CORRECT 3D PLACE ALONG IT.** Moved here from [[A21]], which is otherwise banked for the interstellar-autopilot work. This half needs NO schema change and belongs with the route fix rather than with it: once a route runs star-to-star in 3D, a ship's position along it is an interpolation between two endpoints that already have z. Doing it in the same pass is nearly free; doing it later means re-deriving the same geometry. **The same two traps apply** — use the EXAGGERATED z the star sprites are drawn at rather than raw z, and if the ship marker carries any oriented geometry (a glyph quad, a heading indicator) check it is not yaw-only the way the route glow was. That makes this the first case where the missing third category — a tag that is engine-AUTHORED but not engine-MAINTAINED — has a user-visible consequence rather than being a modelling nicety. **Do not fix this in isolation:** `docs/dev/unified-tagging-design.md` is the live redesign of exactly this lifecycle (system/physics/user sources, `tagLifecycle.ts`), so the third source belongs in that spec, not bolted onto `tagSource`. **Concrete ask for whoever does it:** a source that is written once at creation, freely removable, and re-asserted only if the value it describes is regenerated. Related: [[B10]], [[D2a]]. | **FIXED v2.1.421-beta.** The missing third source is `authored` in `tagLifecycle.ts`: written once at creation, never re-derived, freely removable — which is the concrete ask, verbatim. Provenance now comes from `tagOrigin()` rather than from guessing at the namespace, so the Tags tab groups these under **Generated** with a plain statement that nothing re-creates them, and `physicsTrace` — worse, since it claims to show the working — stops attributing them to a physics layer that never ran. **The bite the entry named is closed too:** typing a real obliquity or rotation period now retires the matching `spin/*-inferred` tag on the spot, because a tag saying "this is a guess" is false the moment the number stops being one. |

| D13 | **Pluto loses its methane wisps once its nitrogen frost is modelled, and real Pluto has methane haze.** Found 2026-08-03 as the single regression in [[B5]]. Pluto's dominant gas is N2, which freezes at 63 K; its surface sits near 40, so the new volatile-frost term correctly lays nitrogen on the ground and takes its albedo **0.299 → 0.579 against a measured Bond albedo of about 0.72** — a large improvement. But the brighter surface then drops it to 36 K, and at that temperature the cloud model no longer forms the methane deck it used to (`structure/cloud-deck=methane wisps` and its virga both go). **Triton, which is the same physics at 39.9 K, KEEPS its methane wisps**, so this is a narrow threshold effect rather than a broken branch — the two differ by about 4 K and land on opposite sides of something. **Where to look:** `deriveCloudDecks`' minimum-fraction / saturation test for a condensate whose own melt point (CH4, 90 K) is far ABOVE the surface temperature — at 36 K methane is not condensing out of the air, it is already on the ground, so arguably the honest answer is that Pluto's methane is frost rather than cloud and the deck SHOULD go. **That is the question to settle**: whether a species far below its freezing point should still be allowed a haze layer (real Pluto's is photochemical tholin haze, which is a different mechanism from condensation and is not modelled at all). Do not simply widen a threshold until the deck returns — decide which mechanism is being claimed. Related: [[B5]], [[B1]]. **ANSWERED 2026-08-11: the mechanism being claimed is CONDENSATION, the engine is applying it correctly, and the deck SHOULD go. No code change, and none wanted.** The entry's own suspicion was right. **IT IS NOT A THRESHOLD EFFECT, which is the part worth knowing** — measured, both bodies clear the `minFraction` gate comfortably (CH4 declares its own 0.0005, not the 0.001 default, and Pluto's capped fraction is 9.145e-4). They differ on something physical instead: **Pluto's air is SATURATED IN METHANE AT THE GROUND and Triton's is not.** Pluto declares ~1% CH4 into an atmosphere that at 36.03 K can hold only 0.091%, so the surface-saturation cap pins it to exactly saturation and `condensationOf` puts the deck's base at level 0 — the surface itself. Triton declares 0.1% into an atmosphere that at 39.89 K can hold 0.92%, so its ground air is UNDER-saturated (surface excess -8.2e-3) and it first saturates at level 7, well aloft: a genuine lofted deck. Pluto's notional deck is then dropped at the `coverage < 0.004` reporting floor, because what little stays suspended above a ground-level base at 1e-5 bar is nothing anyone could resolve. **A cloud whose base is the ground is fog, and methane saturated at the surface of a 36 K world is exactly what "the methane is frost" means** — which the engine also says, correctly and separately, via `volatiles/ices = methane`. Note the two bodies are NOT knife-edge neighbours: Triton clears its cap by 9x. **So the honest reading is that Pluto lost a deck it should never have had, and B5 traded it for an albedo that went 0.299 to 0.579 against a measured 0.72.** **WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM, and it is a FEATURE not a fix:** real Pluto's haze is photochemical tholin — sub-micron particles from N2/CH4 photolysis, in some twenty layers reaching 300 km — and the engine models no photochemistry at all; `deriveCloudDecks` is saturation-driven end to end. Adding it is a physics-session item with its own design, not a threshold to widen, and per this entry's own instruction nothing here was widened. Related: [[B5]], [[B1]], [[D14]]. **FOOTNOTE 2026-08-27, because this entry names a gate that no longer exists:** `cloud.minFraction` was REMOVED under [[B95]] (engine-map **PHY-31**) — it was an abundance floor deleting optically thick decks, our own Saturn's ammonia among them. **THIS ENTRY'S ANSWER IS UNAFFECTED AND WAS CHECKED, not assumed:** its reasoning never rested on the gate — it explicitly measured that both Pluto and Triton cleared it comfortably and located the real difference in surface saturation — and removing the gate changes neither body (the sweep across both bundled starmaps moved exactly one atmosphere, Saturn's). Pluto still correctly has no methane deck, for the reason given here. | **answered 2026-08-11 - working as designed; photochemical haze is a separate FEATURE** |

| C9 | **THE TENTH DUPLICATION, and the worst-placed one: `computeWorldPositions3D` does NOT apply [[C3]]'s satellite reference frame - that rotation exists only in the RENDERER.** Found 2026-08-03 building [[G8]], which had been told to reuse the propagator because "orbital inclinations are now framed correctly after C3". They are not - not in the propagator. **Every copy, located.** The rotation itself was `toParentEquator` at `holo/scene.ts:2710`, private, so nothing outside that file could reach it. It is applied at `holo/scene.ts:2100` for a satellite's live position and again at `holo/scene.ts:2717` inside `buildLocalOrbitRing` for its orbit ring. The tilt-and-ecliptic-gate DECISION is made in two different spellings, at `holo/scene.ts:2032` (gate at the caller) and `holo/scene.ts:2747` (gate inside `buildMoonOrbitRing`), with a third bare read at `holo/scene.ts:1739` that passes an ungated tilt. `physics/worldPositions.ts` has none of it. **So the propagator and the renderer answer "where is this moon" differently, by the parent's axial tilt** - 25.19 deg for Mars, 97.77 for Uranus. Measured: Phobos's orbit normal is 25.2 deg off the reference plane through the framed path and 1.1 deg through the bare propagator, and there is now a test pinning both (`eclipses.spec.ts`, "the satellite reference frame reaches the search"). **Partly unified already:** `toParentEquator` has moved to `system/satelliteFrame.ts` and `scene.ts` imports it, so G8 shares the rotation rather than writing an eleventh copy, and `framedWorldPositions3D` there is the corrected walk. **What remains is the real fix and it is not small:** the frame belongs IN `computeWorldPositions3D` so there is one answer - but the renderer needs parent-RELATIVE offsets for its toytown spread and would have to stop applying the rotation itself, which is a visual change across every moon system and wants its own scoped pass with before/after on the bundled maps. The two gate spellings should collapse into `satelliteTiltRad` at the same time. **Not attempted here on purpose:** `src/lib/physics/**` was off limits to this session, and a renderer change that cannot be eyeballed is not one to make blind. Related: [[C3]], [[C5]], [[G8]]. **FIXED v2.1.410-beta, at the source, and the renderer stopped.** `computeWorldPositions3D` applies the frame itself now - a `frame` op on the 3D walk's ops only, calling `satelliteTiltRad` + `toParentEquator` on each parent-relative offset before it is accumulated. The flat 2D walk deliberately does NOT get it: the orrery propagates omega-only in the reference plane, so there is no out-of-plane axis for an equatorial rotation to tilt into, and 2D is the plan view. **`framedWorldPositions3D` IS DELETED, not kept alongside** - a correction that some callers apply and others do not is the same fault one layer up, which is exactly how this item came to exist. `satelliteFrame.ts` keeps the KNOWLEDGE (the rotation and the gate) and nothing else; `eclipses.ts` calls the propagator directly and no longer knows reference frames exist. **The renderer's placement rotation is gone with `BodyVisual.orbitTiltRad`** - the difference of two world positions is already framed, so double-rotating was the trap and it was avoided. **One call site survives in `scene.ts` and it is not a duplicate:** `buildLocalOrbitRing` samples `propagateState3D` directly, so it holds a raw parent-relative offset rather than a world position - a different input needing the same frame, via the same helper. **The two gate spellings collapsed into `satelliteTiltRad`:** the caller decides, `buildMoonOrbitRing` no longer re-decides. **That closed a latent bug nobody had recorded** - the renderer's test for "satellite" was "not one hop from the root", which makes a planet orbiting a binary's SECONDARY star a satellite and rotates it by that star's tilt. Its inclination is system-framed like any planet's. No shipped map hits it (checked: 20 secondary stars with children across the bundled maps and examples, every one with no tilt or zero), but generation gives stars 0-8 deg via `starTiltFromPack`, so a GENERATED binary would have. **VERIFIED NUMERICALLY over 96 systems in every bundled map and standalone example at three epochs each**, by reproducing the OLD renderer path (bare walk + its own rotation and gate) beside the new one: **the rendered offset is unchanged to 1.1e-10 of the orbit radius**, and that residue is floating-point noise the new path REMOVES rather than adds - the old one recovered a 1e-4 AU offset by subtracting two AU-scale numbers, and this one never does that subtraction. **The world POSITION moves by up to 1.178 AU** (a station orbiting Xygax, host tilt 32.25 deg; Phoebe's station at Saturn moves 0.046 AU) and that is the correction every non-renderer consumer was missing. **G8's eclipse times are unmoved and all 24 of its tests pass unchanged**, for a stated reason: `framedWorldPositions3D` and the framed propagator compute the same thing, so the search sees what it always saw. `tests/output/solar-system-derived.json` is byte-identical - nothing in a derivation pass reads positions. New pins live in `worldPositions.spec.ts`, the frame's own module now, with the control being the same propagator over a system whose host does not lean. **NOT SEEN: the Browser pane does not composite here, so there is no visual check** - the scene module was mounted live in the page against the bundled Sol and driven through Saturn and Uranus without error, but nobody has looked at it.
